question: A 42-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 10-month history of joint pain and stiffness in her wrists and fingers. The symptoms are worse in the morning and improve with activity. Physical examination shows swelling and warmth over the MCP and wrist joints in both hands. An x-ray of the hands is shown. Synovial biopsy from an affected joint would most likely show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "42-year-old woman with joint pain and stiffness" -> "symptoms worse in the morning" -> "indicates possible inflammatory arthritis" -> "swelling and warmth over MCP and wrist joints" -> "suggests synovitis" -> "synovial biopsy likely shows inflammatory changes" -> "proliferation of granulation tissue" -> 85%

CHAIN: "42-year-old woman with joint pain and stiffness" -> "symptoms improve with activity" -> "suggests inflammatory rather than mechanical cause" -> "swelling and warmth over MCP and wrist joints" -> "indicates active inflammation" -> "synovial biopsy would show signs of inflammation" -> "proliferation of granulation tissue" -> 80%

CHAIN: "42-year-old woman with joint pain and stiffness" -> "symptoms worse in the morning" -> "suggests rheumatoid arthritis" -> "swelling and warmth over MCP and wrist joints" -> "indicates synovial inflammation" -> "synovial biopsy likely shows inflammatory cells" -> "proliferation of granulation tissue" -> 90%

CHAIN: "42-year-old woman with joint pain and stiffness" -> "symptoms consistent with rheumatoid arthritis" -> "swelling and warmth over MCP and wrist joints" -> "indicates synovitis" -> "synovial biopsy would show inflammatory process" -> "proliferation of granulation tissue" -> 88%
analysis: The clinical presentation of joint pain and stiffness, particularly in the wrists and fingers, along with morning stiffness that improves with activity, is suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In RA, a synovial biopsy typically shows a proliferation of granulation tissue, which is characteristic of the inflammatory process in this condition. Other options such as monosodium urate crystals and calcium pyrophosphate crystals are associated with gout and pseudogout, respectively, while noncaseating granulomas are seen in conditions like sarcoidosis. Therefore, the most likely finding in a synovial biopsy from an affected joint in this case is proliferation of granulation tissue.
